newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia to draft privatisation plan end March - paper.
newsitem.headline: Serbia to draft privatisation plan end March - paper.

text.p: The Serbian government will submit a draft law on privatisation to the republic's parliament by the end of the month, Belgrade daily Politika reported on Tuesday.
"Privatisation is an important part of our economic strategy and will increase our foreign currency reserves," the paper quoted Dragan Tomic, Serbian minister-coordinator as saying.

"Everyone should chose one of the models offered by the law to be submitted to parliament by the end of March," he said speaking at a meeting with local businessmen in the southern Serbian town of Vranje on Monday.
Key government targets this year included 10-percent growth based on a 14-percent increase in production and a 40-percent rise in exports, the minister said.
Tomic underlined that there would be no new printing of money, and the dinar would remain stable as long as the present government was in power.
He said mass demonstrations in November halted the initial revival in production that followed the lifting of sanctions, but the government expected improvement again when the situation calms down.
"We expect to reach an agreement on the country's return to the international community and the world's financial institutions after which we forsee an inflow of foreign capital," he said.
Tomic also said his previous post as a president of Simpo Holding Company will be filled by Vladimir Arsic. Cabinet members cannot head companies.
